summary: Correct the possessive ending: her bolster, not his
rationale: The cited verse reads u došakayḏa. Its feminine possessor is the woman who tears her clothes and lies down; the example changes -ayḏa to masculine -ayḏe. The edition also translates ihren Pfühl.

summary: Restore the quilt and bolster in the translation
before: on her feather bed, under the pillows
after: under the quilt and her bolster
rationale: The Turoyo has taḥt u=lḥēf w-u=došak-..., under the quilt and bolster. The edition translates unter die Steppdecke und ihren Pfühl. The current English instead introduces a feather bed and replaces the quilt with plural pillows; this changes the objects and their spatial relation.

summary: Restore -no in the quoted rhetorical question mə ḥozeno
rationale: The matching passage reads koḥoze, mə ḥozeno hoh! The glossary has mə=ḥoze and drops the -no ending. Retain the glossary boundary convention but restore the letters present in the corpus.

summary: Translate kul tloṯo arbʕo lalye as a recurring interval
before: for the whole three or four nights
after: and change fields every three or four nights
rationale: The matching corpus has kul tloṯo-arbʕo lalye, every three or four nights. The edition explicitly says alle drei oder vier Nächte auf einem anderen Feld. The current English whole three or four nights loses the recurrence and change of field.

summary: Split the bare imperative madmáx; 152 from the MM 98 sentence

split_examples.translation: bringt sie an einem sauberen Platz unter!

rationale: The Turoyo field contains a separate bare imperative followed by its grammar-page reference, madmáx; 152;, before the sentence with its own translation and MM 98 reference. Split these existing items in the same box: preserve madmáx with reference 152 as an untranslated form, and keep only b-dukṯo naḏ̣əfto madmex-la as the Turoyo of the translated MM 98 example. The matching Hors 2/98 text confirms the latter sentence independently.
The cited edition reads vom Palmsonntag an and repeats Palmsonntag in its explanatory clause. Psalmsonntag is a misspelling of the feast name.

summary: Check the vocative ʕamme against the edition at 6/34
rationale: The glossary starts the quoted words with ʕamme (Tante), but the supplied Turoyo verse has only E, omər, mu sabab d damixət ... and contains no ʕamme. Its German translation nevertheless includes Tante. The corpus transcription may have omitted the vocative, so deleting it from the glossary is not justified without checking the edition.

The subject sie is plural, as shown by gesprochen and sie wollten schlafen in the same sentence. The auxiliary for the coordinated sich lange unterhalten must therefore be hatten. The supplied German verse has the same grammatical slip.
